title: JavaScript and TypeScript
tagline: The language of the web, with types
description: From the basics of the language to typed, structured programs that run in the browser and on the server. The course covers values and control flow, functions, arrays and objects, classes, errors and modules, asynchronous code with promises and async/await, TypeScript's type system, and the browser: the DOM, events, storage and tooling, ending with a complete web app. Practice runs in a sandbox in your browser, with TypeScript type-checked as you type.

milestones.title: First Steps
milestones.blurb: Running JavaScript, values and variables, operators and conversions, strings and template literals, and control flow.

lessons.title: What JavaScript Is and Running It
lessons.summary: JavaScript is the language every web browser runs, and with Node.js it runs on servers and in tools too. This lesson explains where it runs, how it is executed, the console, and how TypeScript relates to it.

lessons.title: Values, Variables and Types
lessons.summary: JavaScript's types - number, string, boolean, undefined, null, bigint, symbol and objects - declaring variables with const and let (and why not var), typeof, and how values are copied or shared.

lessons.title: Operators, Comparisons and Conversions
lessons.summary: Arithmetic and assignment operators, strict versus loose equality, truthiness, the logical operators and the nullish operators ?? and ?., and converting between strings and numbers without surprises.

lessons.title: Strings and Template Literals
lessons.summary: Working with text - template literals with ${} expressions, indexing and length, the most useful string methods, splitting and joining, padding and formatting numbers, and Unicode characters.

lessons.title: Control Flow
lessons.summary: Making decisions and repeating work - if and else, the conditional operator, switch, for loops in their three forms, while and do-while, break and continue, and labelled loops.

milestones.title: Functions and Data
milestones.blurb: Functions and arrow functions, arrays and their methods, objects and destructuring, closures and scope, Maps, Sets and JSON.

lessons.title: Functions
lessons.summary: Function declarations, function expressions and arrow functions, parameters with defaults, rest parameters and spread, returning values, functions as values, and callbacks.

lessons.title: Arrays and Array Methods
lessons.summary: Creating and changing arrays, and the methods that make array code short and clear - map, filter, reduce, find, some and every, includes, sort with a compare function, slice versus splice, flat and flatMap, and which methods change the array.

lessons.title: Objects and Destructuring
lessons.summary: Objects as collections of named values - creating and reading them, dot and bracket access, adding and deleting properties, shorthand and computed names, Object.keys, values and entries, spread and copying, and destructuring objects and arrays.

lessons.title: Scope and Closures
lessons.summary: Where variables live - block scope with let and const, function scope, the scope chain, closures that remember variables, private state with closures, and the classic closure-in-a-loop bug that let fixes.

lessons.title: Maps, Sets and JSON
lessons.summary: Map for key-value data with any key type and reliable ordering, Set for unique values, when to use them instead of plain objects and arrays, grouping with Map and Object.groupBy, and converting data to and from JSON text.

milestones.title: Objects, Errors and Modules
milestones.blurb: Classes, prototypes and this, errors and exceptions, iterators and generators, and modules.

lessons.title: Classes
lessons.summary: Defining classes with constructors, fields and methods, private fields with #, getters and setters, static members, inheritance with extends and super, overriding methods, instanceof, and when a plain object or function is simpler.

lessons.title: Prototypes and this
lessons.summary: How JavaScript objects really share behaviour - the prototype chain under classes, Object.create, own versus inherited properties, the four rules for this, losing this when passing methods, and fixing it with arrow functions and bind.

lessons.title: Errors and Exceptions
lessons.summary: Throwing and catching errors, the built-in error types, finally for clean-up, writing your own error classes, rethrowing what you cannot handle, error causes, validating input at the edges, and returning results instead of throwing.

lessons.title: Iterators and Generators
lessons.summary: What for...of and spread really use - the iteration protocol, making your own objects iterable with Symbol.iterator, generator functions with yield, lazy and infinite sequences, and helpers that combine generators.

lessons.title: Modules
lessons.summary: Splitting a program into files with ES modules - named and default exports, import forms, renaming and namespace imports, module scope and strict mode, live bindings, side effects, CommonJS require in older Node code, and how to organise modules.

milestones.title: Asynchronous JavaScript
milestones.blurb: The event loop and callbacks, promises, async and await, fetching data, timers and concurrency patterns.

lessons.title: The Event Loop and Callbacks
lessons.summary: Why JavaScript code never blocks - one thread, the call stack, the task queue and the event loop, setTimeout and what a delay of 0 means, microtasks, callback-style APIs with error-first callbacks, and why deeply nested callbacks led to promises.

lessons.title: Promises
lessons.summary: A promise as a value that arrives later - its three states, creating one with new Promise, chaining then and catch, returning promises from then, finally, wrapping callback APIs, and combining promises with Promise.all, allSettled, race and any.

lessons.title: async and await
lessons.summary: Writing asynchronous code that reads like ordinary code - async functions always return promises, await pauses only the function, try/catch/finally for errors, running steps in sequence versus in parallel, awaiting in loops, and top-level await.

lessons.title: Fetching Data
lessons.summary: Loading data over HTTP with fetch - responses and status codes, reading JSON and text, why fetch does not reject on 404, sending JSON with POST, headers, query strings with URLSearchParams, timeouts and cancelling with AbortController, and a small API client.

lessons.title: Timers, Debouncing and Concurrency
lessons.summary: setTimeout, setInterval and clearing them, a sleep helper, debounce and throttle for noisy events, timeouts for promises, retrying with backoff, and running async work with a concurrency limit.

milestones.title: TypeScript
milestones.blurb: Basic types, interfaces and type aliases, unions and narrowing, generics, and classes, enums and utility types.

lessons.title: Why TypeScript and Basic Types
lessons.summary: What TypeScript adds to JavaScript and what it does not change, compiling and type-checking, annotating variables, parameters and return values, type inference, arrays and tuples, any versus unknown, null and undefined under strict mode, and reading type errors.

lessons.title: Interfaces and Type Aliases
lessons.summary: Describing the shape of objects with interfaces and type aliases, optional and readonly properties, function types, index signatures and Record, extending and intersecting types, structural typing, and excess property checks.

lessons.title: Unions and Narrowing
lessons.summary: Union types for values that can be one of several things, literal types, narrowing with typeof, instanceof, in and equality checks, discriminated unions with a kind field, exhaustive switches with never, and type guard functions for validating unknown data.

tasks.title: A robot with a discriminated union

lessons.title: Generics
lessons.summary: Writing functions, interfaces and classes that work for any type while keeping type information - type parameters, inference of type arguments, constraints with extends, keyof and indexed access types, default type parameters, and generic containers.

lessons.title: Classes, Enums and Utility Types
lessons.summary: Typed classes with access modifiers, parameter properties, implements and abstract classes, enums and why unions of literals are often better, as const, and the built-in utility types Partial, Required, Pick, Omit, Readonly, Record, ReturnType and Awaited.

milestones.title: The Browser and Projects
milestones.blurb: The DOM, events and forms, storing data in the browser, npm and tooling, and a complete web app.

lessons.title: The DOM
lessons.summary: How a web page is a tree of objects - loading scripts, finding elements with querySelector, reading and changing text, attributes, classes and styles, creating and removing elements, why textContent is safe and innerHTML is not, and rendering a list from data.

lessons.title: Events and Forms
lessons.summary: Reacting to the user - addEventListener, the event object, bubbling and event delegation, preventDefault, keyboard events, forms with submit, FormData and built-in validation, custom validation messages, and keeping handlers small.

lessons.title: Storing Data in the Browser
lessons.summary: Keeping data between visits - localStorage and sessionStorage, storing objects as JSON, handling missing, corrupt and old data with versions, storage limits and errors, cookies in brief, IndexedDB for larger data, and what never to store in the browser.

lessons.title: Tooling
lessons.summary: The tools around a JavaScript project - Node and npm, package.json and scripts, installing packages and semantic version ranges, the lock file, a dev server and bundler with Vite, TypeScript's tsconfig, ESLint and Prettier, testing with Vitest, and building for production.

lessons.title: Project: A Web App
lessons.summary: Putting the course together in a complete browser app - a single state object, actions and a pure update function, rendering from state with escaped HTML, event delegation, saving to localStorage with versions, and how the parts are split into modules and tested.
